bib.title: Chapter 4. MCP Clients: Advanced Use and Best Practices (AI Agents with MCP, O'Reilly early release)

question: How does an MCP client implement logging, sampling, roots, elicitation, multi-model and multi-server support, and which practices make a client production-ready?
contributions: Python SDK client callbacks for logging, sampling, roots and elicitation
Best practices: authentication, resumable connections, pagination

results.claim: Servers may ignore roots, so roots are not a security measure.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote: Roots are not a strong security measure, and should not be used as such.

results.claim: Clients that offer sampling should require human approval before the LLM call and before the reply goes back.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote:
You should implement a HITL workflow to get user approval before sending a
message to the LLM and before returning the response to the server.

results.claim: A client must advertise any capability it supports; in the Python SDK passing the callback does this.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote: you are required to advertise that your client does provide them

results.claim: Elicitation replies are accept, decline or cancel; decline and cancel carry no content.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote:
the client
can respond with one of three types of response types: accept, decline, or cancel.

results.claim: A ClientSessionGroup cannot hold two primitives with the same name; component_name_hook renames to avoid collisions.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote:
you cannot have primitives
with the same name in your ClientSessionGroup

results.claim: Streamable HTTP connections can resume from the last SSE event id.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote:
Luckily, streamable
HTTP connections are resumable

results.claim: Only list methods paginate, via nextCursor.
results.setup: Chapter text on the MCP Python SDK; no experiment
results.quote:
Currently, only the
list functions support pagination

limits: Early-release draft, raw and unedited; no experiments or measurements.
Code examples are simplified: the sampling and roots handlers lack the HITL and validation the chapter says are required.
Written against one Python SDK version; SDK names and spec revisions have likely moved on.
Author name and year are not printed in the PDF text.
practices: Implement HITL approval before and after a sampling request, respect model preferences, rate limit (Supporting Sampling).
Do not treat roots as a security boundary; host application keeps the final say (Supporting Roots).
Roots: validate URIs against path traversal, enforce access controls, monitor accessibility, get user consent (Supporting Roots).
Elicitation: let user accept/decline/cancel, validate against schema, name the requesting server, rate limit (Supporting Elicitations).
Keep the client model-neutral by translating MCP tools to each model family's format in a host-side class (Supporting Multiple Models).
Use ClientSessionGroup for several servers and a name hook for collisions (Using Multiple Servers).
stdio auth: read credentials from environment; streamable HTTP: OAuth 2.1 client library (Security).
Keep session ID and last event ID and send Last-Event-ID to resume (Resuming Connections).
Follow nextCursor to page list results (Paginating Results).

problems: Code listings are truncated at line width in the PDF text; web-page chrome at the end.
Authors, year not printed; first_author from the repo note, not the PDF.
Bug in Example 4-3: roots_result is a list, so 'is None' never fires on an empty list.
Example 4-2 hardcodes model='claude-sonnet-4-0' and ignores modelPreferences and systemPrompt.
Text says a client can connect to only one server, yet Example 4-7 get_resource still checks _connected which the text says was removed.
Text says the server includes Last-Event-ID in a GET; the code sends it from the client as a header.
